traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Myristicaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; leaves evergreen; stipules absent; plants monoecious or dioecious; ovary superior; stems woody; flowers in cymes, in racemes or in heads; perianth tepals; fruit legume; parts of each whorl 3; stamens (2-) 3 to 30; carpels 1. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.fruit_type.note: APweb, Magnoliales page, Myristicaceae (read 2026-10-16): the fruit is a follicle opening along both sides, only exceptionally indehiscent; the current 'legume' follows DELTA's wording for a one-carpel fruit splitting on both sutures, which the vocabulary's follicle fits better.

traits.sexual_system.note: APweb, Magnoliales page, Myristicaceae (read 2026-10-16): the family is characterised as dioecious, with monoecy said to have arisen a few separate times; so dioecious is the usual state and monoecious the exception.
